Sample information : Sample_A



Estimated number of cells
The number of barcodes identified as real cells (not background noise or empty droplets) in the sequencing data. This is estimated using an empty droplet model (EmptyDrops) after merging cell barcodes from the same droplet. Values higher or lower than expected may indicate inaccurate cell counting, cell lysis, or issues in droplet generation.
Median UMI counts per cell
The median number of unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) detected per cell among all identified cells.
Median genes per cell
The median number of unique genes with detectable expression in each cell.
Mean reads per cell
The average number of raw sequencing reads per cell, calculated by dividing the total raw reads by the number of identified cells.

Beads to cells


(left) Barcode Rank Plot
In the library, transcripts from the same cell are grouped under a unified cell ID, each tagged with unique molecular identifiers (UMIs). However, RNA from ambient sources or dying cells may also be captured during library preparation. This barcode rank plot visualizes the distribution of total UMI counts per cell ID (x-axis: cell ID rank; y-axis: UMI count, both in log scale). Cell IDs with higher UMI counts (on the left) are more likely to represent real cells, while lower-count IDs (on the right) are often background. Blue points indicate high-confidence cells, gray points represent background (e.g., empty droplets), and the blue gradient region marks a transitional zone identified by an ambient RNA model. Hovering over each point reveals its rank, UMI count, and the percentage of real cells in its neighborhood, aiding in the distinction between true cells and noise.
(right) Bead Count Distribution
This plot displays the distribution of barcoded bead counts per droplet among identified real cells. While the number of beads per droplet is theoretically expected to follow a Poisson distribution, deviations may occur due to factors such as low RNA capture or inefficient bead merging. The distribution is affected by cell filtering thresholds and dynamically updates accordingly. If most droplets contain only one bead, it is advisable to check whether the oligo library has sufficient sequencing depth (recommended >50M reads) and whether it is properly matched to the cDNA library, as these factors can impact overall data quality and cell recovery.
Summary


Mean reads per cell
The average number of raw sequencing reads per cell, calculated by dividing the total raw reads by the number of identified cells.
Mean UMI counts per cell
The average number of unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) detected per cell, assessing gene expression levels in single-cell sequencing. Depends on cell type and sequencing depth; lower than expected may indicate shallow sequencing or sample/library quality issues.
Median UMI counts per cell
The median number of unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) detected per cell, assessing gene expression levels in single-cell sequencing. Depends on cell type and sequencing depth; lower than expected may indicate shallow sequencing or sample/library quality issues.
Total genes detected
The total number of unique genes detected across all cells, indicating the overall gene diversity captured in the dataset.
Mean genes per cell
The average number of genes detected per cell. Depends on cell type and sequencing depth; lower than expected may be due to biological reasons (low transcriptional diversity) or indicate low sequencing depth or library complexity.
Median genes per cell
The median number of genes detected per cell. Depends on cell type and sequencing depth; lower than expected may be due to biological reasons (low transcriptional diversity) or indicate low sequencing depth or library complexity.
Sequencing saturation
The proportion of UMIs that originate from already-observed UMIs, indicating how close the library is to being fully sequenced. Higher saturation suggests that additional sequencing may not yield much new information.
Fraction reads in cells
The proportion of reads that are uniquely mapped to the transcriptome and associated with a valid cell barcode, indicating the efficiency of cell capture.
Violin Plot
A violin plot illustrating the distribution of nFeature (number of genes detected) and nCount (number of UMIs) across all cells, providing insights into data quality and variability.

Sequencing


Number of reads
The total number of raw reads generated from the sequencing run.
Valid barcodes
The fraction of reads with barcodes that match the whitelist after correction. High values indicate good barcode quality and effective correction.
Corrected barcodes
The fraction of reads whose barcodes were corrected to match the whitelist due to initial mismatches.
Valid UMIs
The fraction of reads with valid UMIs, which are sequences without ambiguous bases (Ns) and are not homopolymers. High values suggest good UMI quality.
Q30 bases in barcode
The fraction of bases in cell barcodes with a quality score (Q-score) ≥ 30, indicating high sequencing quality for barcodes.
Q30 bases in UMI
The fraction of bases in UMIs with a quality score (Q-score) ≥ 30, reflecting reliable UMI sequencing.
Q30 bases in rna/index read
The fraction of bases in the reads with a quality score (Q-score) ≥ 30, assessing overall read quality.

Mapping & Annotation


Reads mapped to genome
The proportion of sequencing reads aligned to any position in the reference genome, including both uniquely mapped and multi-mapped reads. This metric reflects overall alignment efficiency. Lower values may indicate poor sample quality, mismatches with the reference genome, or sequencing errors.
Reads mapped confidently to genome
The proportion of reads reliably aligned to the reference genome, primarily consisting of uniquely mapped reads. Multi-mapped reads are retained if they align to a single exonic locus alongside one or more non-exonic loci. This metric indicates the reliability and biological relevance of read placement. Lower proportions may result from poor sequencing quality or mismatches between the sample and the reference genome.
Reads mapped confidently to transcriptome
The proportion of reads uniquely mapped to the transcriptome and assigned to a single gene. For exonic reads, alignments must match annotated splice junctions (intronic reads are excluded). These reads directly contribute to UMI counting and are a critical indicator of library quality. Higher values indicate greater specificity and mRNA capture reliability; lower values may reflect incomplete transcriptome annotations or poor sample quality.
Reads mapped to mitochondrial genome
Percentage of reads aligned to the mitochondrial genome. High values may indicate mitochondrial RNA enrichment or stressed/damaged cells.
Reads mapped confidently to exonic regions
The proportion of reads confidently aligned to annotated exonic regions. A read is classified as exonic if at least 50% of its sequence overlaps with an exon.
Reads mapped confidently to intronic regions
The proportion of reads confidently aligned to annotated intronic regions. Reads are classified as intronic if they do not meet exonic criteria but intersect with annotated introns. These reads often originate from unspliced pre-mRNA or nuclear RNA.
Reads mapped confidently to intergenic regions
The proportion of reads confidently aligned to genomic regions not annotated as part of any gene (intergenic). Reads are classified as intergenic if they meet neither exonic nor intronic criteria. Elevated values may suggest non-specific amplification during library preparation or incomplete reference annotation.
Reads mapped antisense to gene
The proportion of reads confidently mapped to the transcriptome but aligned in the antisense orientation relative to annotated genes. These may arise from technical noise, natural antisense transcripts, or insufficient strand specificity during library preparation.
Include introns
Includes reads that map to intronic regions during gene expression quantification. Including introns can significantly increase the number of UMIs and genes detected, especially in single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq).
Note
All proportions are calculated using the total number of raw sequencing reads as the denominator to ensure consistency and comparability across metrics.

Cluster


Left
Cell type clustering plot generated using the Louvain algorithm to group cells with similar gene expression profiles, visualized through UMAP dimensionality reduction where different colors represent distinct cell clusters or potential cell types.
Right
UMI expression intensity plot showing total UMI counts per cell on the same UMAP coordinate system, with a color gradient from low to high expression levels for effective quality control assessment.
Marker


Table
The table shows the top 30 differentially expressed genes for each cluster. Here a differential expression test was performed between each cluster and the rest of the sample for each gene. The p-value is a measure of the statistical significance of the expression difference, the smaller the P value, the closer to the theoretical value. Avg_log2FC is log fold-chage of the average expression between the markers for every cluster compared to all remaining cells.

Cell Annotation


Predicted cell type
Predicted cell types were assigned based on correlation with established reference atlases: scHCL (Single-cell Human Cell Landscape) for human samples and scMCA (Single-cell Mouse Cell Atlas) for mouse samples. The annotation relies on Pearson correlation between individual cell expression profiles and reference cell types. UMAP plots display the predicted cell identities, with each color representing a distinct cell type. These results are intended for reference only and should be interpreted in the context of experimental and biological background. Annotation accuracy may vary depending on reference coverage and sample diversity. For non-human/mouse species, automated annotation is not currently supported. Users are encouraged to complement this initial annotation with marker gene expression analysis to ensure biological relevance.
Saturation


Left: Sequencing Saturation Curve
This plot shows how sequencing saturation varies with increasing sequencing depth, measured as mean reads per cell (downsampled). Saturation is calculated as 1 minus the ratio of unique UMI counts to total UMI counts, reflecting library complexity. A saturation value nearing 1.0 (100%) indicates that most mRNA transcripts have been captured. A plateau in the curve suggests that additional sequencing yields minimal new information, aiding in assessing whether the current depth is sufficient and cost-effective.
Right: Median Genes per Cell Curve
This plot illustrates the median number of genes detected per cell across different sequencing depths. It highlights transcriptome complexity and per-cell sequencing coverage. A flattening curve near the observed depth indicates diminishing returns in gene detection with further sequencing.
